summary: This diff adds three new deterministic audit pipelines (api-contract via Spectral, metadata via ajv-cli, integration via schemathesis), three hand-authored OpenAPI 3.1 contracts, three metadata JSON Schemas, a drizzle-comment extraction helper, and a phase-plan close-out script/status update. The code is well-structured: parameterized SQL throughout (no injection risk), no shell=True subprocess calls, no secrets or credentials embedded, proper file-locking for the shared sqlite DB matching the existing audit_pipeline_security.py convention, and honest handling of partial coverage (schemathesis only ran live against veda-advisors; compliance-tracker/projexa are explicitly recorded as skipped rather than faked). Tool-quirk workarounds (Spectral's malformed JSON+summary stdout, ajv-cli's asymmetric stdout/stderr split) are documented and handled correctly. The diff touches no migrations, schema.sql/prisma, auth/, payment/billing/RLS paths, .env files, or .github/workflows/** -- confirmed via path grep -- and consists entirely of new, additive files, matching the tier1 definition. One minor, non-blocking nit: audit_pipeline_metadata.py's check_openapi_info_blocks() computes artifact_path via os.path.relpath(path, start=os.path.join(_HERE, '..', '..')), one directory level higher than the repo root other artifact paths use elsewhere in this same file and in audit_pipeline_api_contract.py, which will produce an inconsistent-looking (but harmless) artifact_path string like '<repo-dirname>/ai-os/openapi/<file>' instead of 'ai-os/openapi/<file>' for metadata findings on OpenAPI info blocks.
issues: Minor: audit_pipeline_metadata.py's check_openapi_info_blocks() uses a relpath base one directory too high (os.path.join(_HERE, '..', '..')), producing an artifact_path inconsistent with the 'ai-os/openapi/...' convention used elsewhere in this same diff. Cosmetic only -- does not affect correctness of findings, DB writes, or security.
